short: Forkhead box (FOX) proteins are a family of about 50 human transcription factors that bind DNA as monomers through a ~100-residue winged-helix domain, named for the two loops, or wings, that flank its three-helix core. Nearly all of them read the same seven-base element, RYAAAYA, usually written GTAAACA or, on the opposite strand, TGTTTAC. The family includes the FOXA pioneer factors that engage nucleosomal DNA and open liver, prostate and breast enhancers; the insulin- and stress-controlled FOXO proteins; FOXC, FOXE, FOXG and FOXL factors needed for eye, thyroid, forebrain and ovary development; and the proliferation factor FOXM1. Because the DNA-contacting residues are almost invariant across the family, a forkhead match tells you that a FOX protein could bind there, but rarely which one.
long:
## The factors

The human genome carries about 50 forkhead box genes in 19 subfamilies, FOXA through FOXS. Each
encodes one copy of the forkhead (winged-helix) domain: roughly 100 residues in which three
alpha-helices pack against a short three-stranded beta-sheet. Helix H3 lies in the major groove
and supplies the base-specific contacts, while two extended loops - wing 1, between strands
beta2 and beta3, and wing 2 at the C-terminus - fold over the phosphate backbone and reach into
the flanking minor groove. The first co-crystal structure, of HNF-3gamma (FOXA3) on DNA, showed
that this fold is essentially that of linker histone H5 and that it bends DNA by about 13
degrees. Binding is monomeric in the usual case, but FOXO1 (and, in the same assays, FOXO3,
FOXM1 and FOXI1) also homodimerizes on a palindromic element using wing 1. Expression ranges
from near-ubiquitous (FOXK1/2, FOXO1/3, FOXJ3) to sharply restricted: FOXA1-3 in endoderm-
derived epithelia, FOXE1 in thyroid, FOXG1 in telencephalon, FOXL2 in granulosa cells and
eyelid, FOXI1 in inner ear and renal intercalated cells, FOXM1 in cycling cells.

## The motif

The literature consensus is RYAAAYA (R = A/G, Y = C/T), seven base pairs, most often realized as
GTAAACA; the medoid model of the 106 collected here is exactly GTAAACA, matching the databases.
Specificity comes almost entirely from H3 contacts to the central AAA run and the following
pyrimidine, several of them water-mediated, which is why that core tolerates so little variation
and the flanks so much. The FOXO field calls the same element the DAF-16 binding element, core
TTGTTTAC, and distinguishes it from the weaker insulin-response sequence in the IGFBP1 promoter.
Longer models in the data are one of three things: an extended monomeric site with AT-rich
flanks (HOCOMOCO FOXA1, TTGTTTACTTAA); a perfect palindrome, GTAAATATTTAC, which is two RYAAAYA
half-sites head-to-head with no spacer and corresponds to the wing-1 homodimer site (HOCOMOCO
FOXD3, FOXD2, FOXB1, FOXC1; CIS-BP FOXC2); or a composite with a partner, as in the JASPAR
models FOXO1::ELK1, FOXO1::ELK3, FOXO1::ELF1 and FOXO1::FLI1, where most of the information
content is the ETS GGAA core, not the forkhead site. Two members are real exceptions. FOXM1
models carry almost no information (2.1 bits in CIS-BP) because FOXM1 reaches chromatin mainly
through cofactors and non-canonical sequences. FOXH1 (FAST-1/FAST-2) models read AATCCACA,
equivalently TGTGGATT - the activin/Smad response element - and not RYAAAYA at all. Otherwise
FOXA, FOXB, FOXC, FOXD, FOXI, FOXK, FOXL, FOXO, FOXQ, FOXR and FOXS are not separable by
sequence.

## Where it acts

Forkhead sites are AT-rich and enhancer-biased: depleted from CpG-island promoters, enriched in
distal tissue-specific elements, and frequently on nucleosomal rather than naked DNA. FOXA1 and
FOXA2 bind a nucleosomal site that overlaps the linker-histone position, displace H1, and hold
liver enhancers in an accessible but nucleosome-occupied state. ChIP-seq typically recovers tens
of thousands of FOXA1 sites per cell type, most of them distal, and which ones are used depends
on the partner present: androgen receptor in prostate, estrogen receptor alpha and GATA3 in
luminal breast, HNF4A and CEBP in liver. FOXA1 is required for almost all ER-chromatin contacts
and for tamoxifen-dependent ER activity. FOXO sites sit at insulin- and oxidative-stress-
responsive promoters and enhancers (IGFBP1, G6PC, SOD2) and are switched off by AKT-driven
nuclear export, not by loss of the site. RYAAAYA is short - with two degenerate positions it is
expected on the order of three million times in a 3.1 Gb double-stranded genome - so occupancy
is set by chromatin and partners, not by the element.

## Biology and disease

Forkhead loss-of-function is usually severe. FOXC1 mutations cause Axenfeld-Rieger malformations
and early-onset glaucoma; FOXL2 mutations cause blepharophimosis-ptosis-epicanthus inversus
syndrome, and the recurrent FOXL2 C134W substitution is present in most adult granulosa cell
tumors; FOXE1 variants affect thyroid development; FOXG1 mutations produce a Rett-like
encephalopathy. FOXA1 is the clearest cancer story. It is altered in roughly a third of prostate
cancers, and the most common class of activating mutation clusters inside the wing-2 loop of the
forkhead domain, increasing chromatin mobility and driving a luminal androgen-receptor program;
other classes truncate the C-terminus or rearrange the locus. FOXA1 is also amplified or mutated
in breast, bladder and salivary tumors and sets the response to endocrine therapy. FOXM1 is
overexpressed in most carcinomas and drives cell-cycle gene expression.

## Reading a hit

A GTAAACA/TGTTTAC match identifies a forkhead site, not a forkhead protein. All of FOXA, FOXO,
FOXK, FOXC and FOXD read this element with the same residues, the models in all four databases
collapse onto one cluster (cohesion 0.78, no member with out-of-family nearest neighbors), and
the archetype names make the point explicitly: AC0042 is "FOXA/FOXB", AC0039 is "FOXD/FOXK",
AC0093 is "FOXC/HOXA". Deciding which FOX protein is involved requires expression data, ChIP, or
a partner site. The element is common enough to occur millions of times by chance, so a single
match in a region of unknown function is weak evidence. Prefer the in vitro models when you need
"this protein binds this sequence": 24 of the 30 HOCOMOCO entries here carry HT-SELEX or methyl-
HT-SELEX evidence (S or M in the fourth field), and only six are ChIP-only. Treat the FOXO1::ETS
and FOXJ2::ELF1 composite models as ETS motifs with a forkhead flank, and treat FOXM1 and FOXH1
models as not representing RYAAAYA.
caveats: High confidence that a match is a forkhead site; very low confidence about which of the ~50 FOX proteins binds it. Sequence cannot separate FOXA from FOXO, FOXC, FOXD, FOXI, FOXK, FOXL or FOXQ, and the Vierstra archetype names (FOXA/FOXB, FOXD/FOXK, FOXC/FOXK) reflect that rather than resolving it. The element is short and AT-rich, so it occurs millions of times by chance; treat matches as candidates that need chromatin or expression evidence. Two labels in this family do not represent RYAAAYA: FOXM1 models are near-uninformative, and FOXH1 models are the activin/Smad response element. Four CIS-BP entries are mouse-derived (FOXJ1, FOXM1, and the inferred FOXS1 and FOXB2 models at 79% and 93% DBD identity).
